title: The Gāyatrī with five faces and ten hands

words.meaning: with the hues of pearl, coral, gold, sapphire-blue and white
whose crown has the moon and jewels set in it
whose self is the syllables that carry the meaning of reality
the boon-giving and fearlessness gestures, the goad and the whip

samasa.members: मुक्ता + विद्रुम + हेम + नील + धवळ + छाया
samasa.vigraha: मुक्ताविद्रुमहेमनीलधवळानां छाया इव छाया येषां तैः
samasa.meaning: having the hues of pearl, coral, gold, blue and white

morphology.note: S writes the Vedic ळ for intervocalic ḍ (धवळ = dhavala, white) and doubles ch after a short vowel.

translation.literal: With faces of pearl, coral, gold, blue and white hue, three-eyed, endowed; whose crown has the moon and jewels set in it; whose self is the syllables of the meaning of reality — the Gāyatrī, bearing in her hands the boon and fearlessness gestures, the goad and the whip, a white skull-bowl, a mace, a conch, a discus and a pair of lotuses, I worship.
translation.readable: I worship the Gāyatrī: five faces, pearl, coral, gold, blue and white, each with three eyes; the moon and jewels in her crown; her very self the syllables that carry the truth; in her ten hands the gestures of boon and fearlessness, the goad, the whip, a white skull-bowl, a mace, the conch, the discus and two lotuses.

meaning: The general meditation on the goddess of the Gāyatrī before the japa, in both witnesses. She has five faces, each a different colour — pearl, coral, gold, blue and white — and each three-eyed; the moon and jewels are set in her crown; and she is described as made of the syllables that carry the meaning of reality, that is, as the mantra itself. Her ten hands hold the attributes listed in the second half.
in_the_rite: Step dhyāna of the Gāyatrī japa, all three services, before the time-specific verse (M) or yo devaḥ savitā (S).

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: Śārdūlavikrīḍita metre: four pādas of nineteen syllables.

notes.label: direct
notes.text: M reads the second pāda युक्तां इन्दु-कला-निबद्ध-मकुटां, the digit of the moon bound in the crown (with इदु for इन्दु); see corrections.json.

flags.text: S has no danda between the pādas, so the text is one line and त्रीक्षणैः युक्ताम् (the end of the first pāda and the start of the second) stands unjoined within it; the padaccheda rejoins into त्रीक्षणैर्युक्तामिन्दु… The fix is either the joined spelling त्रीक्षणैर्युक्तामिन्दु… or dandas at the pāda ends (the padaccheda would then be four lines).
